items.title: India Two-Wheeler Sales, Exports Cross 1.52 Crore In H1 FY 2027
items.summary: Domestic two-wheeler sales grew 17.63% during April–September 2026, while exports expanded faster at 31.86%, taking combined factory dispatch past 1.52 crore units.
items.text: India’s combined domestic two-wheeler sales and exports crossed 1.52 crore units in H1 FY2027, growing 20.35% year-on-year. Motorcycles contributed 96,93,362 units, while scooters crossed 53 lakh units and grew faster at 29.82%. Mopeds added 3,00,252 units. Domestic sales reached 1,20,86,812 units, up 17.63% from 1,02,75,298 units in April–September 2025. Exports stood at 32,07,357 units, growing 31.86% over 24,32,412 units. Combined domestic sales and exports reached 1,52,94,169 units, an increase of approximately 20.35%. Hero Splendor retained first position with 21,30,637 units, growing 19.69%. It added 3,50,556 units year-on-year, the largest absolute gain among the leading domestic entries. Honda Activa followed with 14,82,917 units, up 15.12%. Together, Splendor and Activa accounted for nearly 30% of domestic two-wheeler sales. Also Read – Top 50 Motorcycles Domestic Sales H1 FY 2027 . Honda Shine 125/SP125 ranked third with 9,65,571 units, growing 11.09%, followed by TVS Jupiter at 8,29,725 units, up 15.63%. Bajaj Pulsar completed the top five with 6,33,015 units, although volumes declined 6.86%. Hero HF Deluxe also recorded a decline, falling 16.38% to 4,42,827 units. Suzuki Access grew 10.04% to 4,33,180 units, while TVS Apache increased 22.90% to 3,34,347 units. XL100 and iQube completed the top ten with 2,92,920 units and 2,74,304 units, respectively. items.summary: India’s motorcycle exports grew 31.83% during April–September 2026, with Boxer and Star City together contributing nearly 46% of overseas shipments.
items.text: India’s motorcycle exports reached 27,64,662 units in the first half of FY2027, up 31.83% from 20,97,158 units in April–September 2025. items.summary: The Monster V2 Dark minimises theatricality while stripping the Monster down to its dark essentials, with no mechanical changes.
items.text: Ducati has launched the Monster V2 Dark in global markets, priced at EUR 10,990 (or Rs. 11.69 lakh). The Monster was launched in August 2026, the next chapter in the Monster model's storied history. The Monster V2 Dark will serve as the entry-level model, losing out on a few key features while also offering a minimalist, yet sinister blacked-out design. The Monster was Ducati's first street naked motorcycle, launched in 1992. Since then, the Monster has gone through multiple iterations while retaining its core ethos of simplicity and accessibility. The Monster V2 Dark takes a step further, offering the Monster V2 in a proverbially stripped-down variant, finished in Ducati Dark livery. The aesthetic differences go beyond skin-deep, too. Underneath the jet-black bodywork, Ducati has left the frame, exhaust endcaps, and intake snorkel unpainted, contrasting against the black paintwork. The rims are now all-black, losing out on the red highlights found on the standard model. The seat has been changed slightly too, with a uniform choice of material throughout the seat; the Monster Dark also loses out on the rear seat cowl that buyers would normally get as standard equipment. Interestingly, the Monster Dark also loses out on the LED sequential turn indicators from the standard bike, while the Ducati Quick Shift (DQS) bi-directional quickshifter has become an optional accessory. items.summary: The Harley-Davidson X350 T will be powered by a 349cc, air/oil-cooled engine, which will be a downsized version of the 440cc motor from the X440 T.
items.text: - Likely to be powered by a downsized 349cc version of the 440cc motor - Will benefit from the lower 18 per cent GST rates The Harley-Davidson X350 T has been spied undisguised at a dealership, hinting at its impending launch. The X350 T is expected to share the platform, chassis, cycle parts and styling with the Harley-Davidson X440 T . However, it will get a smaller 349cc engine to benefit from the lower GST rates. It is important to note that the India-spec X350 T is different from the China-spec X350. The latter uses a Benelli-sourced parallel-twin engine, whereas the X350 T is expected to use a downsized version of the single-cylinder engine from the X440 T. While the X440 T uses a 440cc, single-cylinder motor, the Harley-Davidson X350 T is expected to be powered by a 349cc motor. This will allow Harley-Davidson to position it in the sub-350cc category, which attracts 18 per cent GST compared to the 40 per cent applicable on the X 440T. Similar to what Bajaj, Triumph and KTM have done with their respective 400cc engine platforms, we expect Harley-Davidson to follow a similar route by reducing the stroke length while retaining the bore. items.title: SHAD Unveils Terra Crash Bars for BMW R 1300 GS
items.summary: SHAD is expanding its Terra adventure range into motorcycle protection with upper and lower crash bars for the BMW R 1300 GS. Possible India availability after EICMA 2026.
items.text: SHAD Terra crash bars for the BMW R 1300 GS are set to make their show debut at EICMA 2026. This is an important expansion of the Spanish accessory maker’s adventure-focused Terra range. Until now Terra has largely been associated with panniers, top boxes and soft luggage. The addition of motorcycle protection takes the range into a new category and SHAD has chosen one of the most established large adventure motorcycles as its first application. There’s two separate protection systems for the BMW R 1300 GS. Upper Crash Bars are designed to protect the fuel tank, radiator and upper bodywork. The Lower Crash Bars concentrate on the engine, crankcase or oil sump area and exhaust headers. This modular arrangement is useful because owners can choose the degree of protection they need. Although the upper bars require the corresponding lower crash bars to be installed first. Both assemblies are made from AISI 304 stainless steel. SHAD uses 25mm-diameter tubing with a 2mm wall thickness, with the structure designed to provide high strength without adding unnecessary width around the motorcycle. The bars mount directly to the R 1300 GS ’ existing chassis mounting points, meaning installation does not require cutting or drilling the motorcycle. You can pick between two finishes. items.summary: Nitin Gadkari proposes a 20% speeding margin on expressways, which could mean a 144 km/hr challan threshold on roads with a 120 km/hr limit.
items.text: Union Minister for Road Transport and Highways Nitin Gadkari has proposed allowing motorists to exceed prescribed speed limits by up to 20 percent before being issued speeding challans on expressways. The suggestion could effectively raise the enforcement threshold to 144 km/hr on stretches where the maximum permitted speed is 120 km/hr. Speaking at the Confederation of Indian Industry’s (CII) National Conference on Highways of India’s Future, Gadkari said he had instructed officials not to issue notices to motorists travelling at speeds of up to 120 km/hr. He added that a 20 percent margin could be considered beyond the prescribed limit, with challans issued for violations exceeding that threshold. If implemented on expressways with a 120 km/hr speed limit, the proposed margin would translate into an enforcement threshold of 144 km/hr. However, the proposal does not amount to an increase in the legal speed limit. Motorists are still required to adhere to the posted speed restrictions, and any change in enforcement policy would need to be formally communicated by the authorities. Gadkari warns against poor highway construction Apart from discussing speeding enforcement, the minister raised concerns about the quality of highway construction and maintenance. He warned contractors and consultants responsible for substandard work that they could face strict action, including blacklisting, financial penalties and restrictions on future projects. Hero MotoCorp has announced a four-day retail campaign, ‘Herotsav’, from November 1 to 4, as part of its nationwide festive initiative, ‘Hero Sang Tyohar Hai Har Kahin’. The campaign will offer customers a range of retail benefits, including financing of up to 100% of the vehicle cost, EMIs starting at Rs 2,222 and zero-interest financing on scooters. Other benefits include credit card cashback of up to Rs 10,000 and corporate discounts of up to Rs 6,000 on select models. Customers will also get an opportunity to win Hero two-wheelers and gold coins, along with other assured rewards. The initiative follows the introduction of 12 new and updated models across Hero MotoCorp’s motorcycle and scooter portfolios. The company said these launches had contributed to increased customer enquiries and dealership footfalls during the festive period. "Herotsav is our way of turning this festive enthusiasm into an even more rewarding experience—with special offers and exciting benefits for those looking to bring home a Hero two-wheeler," said Ashutosh Varma, Chief Business Officer, India Business Unit, Hero MotoCorp. Customers can avail of the offers at authorised Hero MotoCorp dealerships or through the company's digital retail platform. The benefits will be available between November 1 and 4, 2026.

items.title: Amazon India Records Sixfold Rise in Two-Wheeler Sales During Festive Season So Far
items.summary: Amazon India records a sixfold rise in two-wheeler sales during Great Indian Festival 2026, driven by Tier-2/3 cities and 13.5x commuter motorcycle growth.
items.text: The e-commerce major reports accelerated online purchases, driven by non-metro demand. Amazon India has reported a sixfold increase in two-wheeler sales compared to its average-day pace since the start of its 'Great Indian Festival 2026' campaign. Non-metro locations accounted for over 60 percent of total two-wheeler sales during the period, led by Tier-2 and Tier-3 cities including Surat, Kota, Visakhapatnam, Bhubaneswar, Prayagraj, and Ludhiana. Commuter motorcycles experienced the sharpest expansion, growing at 13.5 times their average-day volume. Electric two-wheelers grew at eight times their baseline pace, while premium motorcycles recorded a 2.5-fold increase. "More customers than ever are starting their purchase on Amazon.in, researching and comparing their next bike, and this festive season the trend has accelerated sharply," said Aman Deep Lohan, Director, Home, Kitchen and Outdoors, Amazon India.

items.text: More details of the bike have been revealed The bike looks close to the final production-spec avatar Expected to launch in India sometime early next year Bajaj is gearing up to enter the affordable adventure motorcycle space, and its upcoming ADV has been spotted testing once again. The latest photographs reveal several details that were previously difficult to make out, giving us a better idea of what the motorcycle could offer when it finally makes its debut. The latest spy shots reveal a rectangular TFT instrument console that appears similar to the display seen on newer Pulsar models. While the information layout remains unclear, the screen itself is clearly visible from the rider’s seat. The switchgear, however, features some differences compared to the latest Pulsars. The right-hand switchgear appears to incorporate a headlight control slider, while the left-hand cluster gets an additional switch at the top. A raised handlebar, conventional mirrors and handguards complete the cockpit setup. At the front, the Bajaj Adventure bike gets an angular headlight. A prominent front beak sits below the headlight, giving it the familiar ADV silhouette. Unlike larger touring-oriented adventure motorcycles, the Bajaj test bike appears to feature a compact headlight cowl rather than a tall windscreen. items.text: October 30, 2026: Royal Enfield's first electric motorcycle, the Flying Flea C6, is now available in another Indian city. However, Royal Enfield has not announced any Pune-specific pricing or special offers. The Royal Enfield Flying Flea C6 comes with a 3.91 kWh battery pack. events.text: In his monthly radio programme ‘Mann ki Baat’, Prime Minister Narendra Modi highlighted conservation efforts across the country, including the return of elephants to Assam’s Sonai Rupai Wildlife Sanctuary and the pygmy hog population rising from six to over 190. The pygmy hog was believed to be extinct by the mid-20th century. In Assam, the Pygmy Hog Conservation Programme was launched in 1995. A year later, six pygmy hogs were taken out of Assam’s grasslands to Manas National Park. Conservationists feared that their dwindling numbers could lead to extinction if they were not bred in captivity. The pygmy hog depends significantly on dense grasslands to feed. However, with the burning of grasslands and their conversion into tea estates brought down their numbers. Since 1996, there has been a 32-fold increase in the numbers of pygmy hogs. Since 2020, six groups of pygmy hogs have been released into the Manas National Park. Earlier this year, the Standing Committee on National Board for Wildlife (SC-NBWL) included the pygmy hog in the list of critically endangered species so that it receives focused conservation support under the Centrally Sponsored Scheme of Integrated Development of Wildlife Habitats (CSS-IDWH). The scheme provides financial assistance to states to protect species under a wildlife recovery programme. events.summary: Recall 0193, KBA 16507R: 2,453 Harleys in Germany, 116,714 worldwide. Street Glide, Road Glide, Breakout and Fat Boy. Oil may escape at the dipstick.
events.text: Harley-Davidson is recalling motorcycles worldwide where the vent hole in the air filter box’s base plate may be blocked by plastic. This causes pressure to build up in the crankcase. If the dipstick is pulled out without allowing the pressure to escape slowly first, oil may spray out of the filler neck. The recall has the manufacturer code 0193. It is listed with the NHTSA as Campaign 26V270 and with Germany’s Federal Motor Transport Authority (KBA) under reference number 16507R. One injury has been reported. As of October 6, 2026. U.S. figures from the NHTSA, figures for Germany and worldwide from the Federal Motor Transport Authority (KBA). Harley-Davidson operates a public recall lookup service based on the VIN. No registration or customer account is required. It also recognizes German motorcycles; we tested this with the VIN of a Harley registered in Germany, and the system returned the active recall 0193. The search feature is only available on the U.S. Harley website; the German site does not offer this option. Your VIN is located on the steering head, on a sticker on the right front frame tube, and in field E of the vehicle registration certificate. The base plate of the air filter box, part number 29000373, has a vent through which gases are expelled from the crankcase. events.title: Yamaha R2 Teased Again Before Launch
events.summary: The latest teaser shows chiselled and layered body panels of the motorcycle with the Yamaha logo.
events.text: Yamaha has released another teaser of its upcoming sportbike, which is likely to be the R2 . Pre-bookings for the bike have already opened, and the official launch is scheduled to take place in two days, on 27 August, 2026. The latest teaser shows chiselled and layered body panels of the motorcycle with the Yamaha logo. Concrete details about the R2 are not available yet, and we have only been doing guesswork so far. The assumption is that the motorcycle will be powered by an enlarged version of the R15’s 155cc, liquid-cooled engine and will produce power and torque. A safe guess would be around 25bhp and 20Nm. Things like a six-speed gearbox, assist and slipper clutch, and a quick shifter (perhaps optional) will certainly be available. The R15, for your reference, makes 18.1bhp and 14.2Nm. The R15 is already a heavily loaded motorcycle in terms of technology, and we believe the R2 will take things a step further. It might come equipped with goodies like ride modes and cruise control. subs.headline: Royal Enfield teases the Himalayan 750 on video ahead of its expected EICMA 2026 debut
subs.text: Royal Enfield has released an official teaser video for the Himalayan 750, its first Himalayan on the new 750cc platform. The bike is expected to make its debut at EICMA 2026 in Milan.

trends_summary.headline: Riders search for EICMA 2026 bikes, Harley's Sprint 440 and Ducati prices
trends_summary.text: Searches for 'eicma 2026 upcoming motorcycles' broke out today, as the Himalayan 750 teaser and India-linked line-ups made news. Harley's Sprint 440 and Hero's Karizma XMR 250 held 5000+ searches this week, and 'ducati bike price' rose 160% after the Monster Dark unveil.

trending.why: Leaked pictures suggest Sprint 440 production has started; Autocar India expects its India launch after the EICMA 2026 debut.
Hero said it will refresh the Karizma range; Autocar India expects the long overdue XMR 250, seen undisguised several times.
Riders want to know which bikes Milan will bring to India: the Himalayan 750 has been teased on video and Rushlane lists the India-linked models expected.
Ducati unveiled the Monster Dark today; the standard Monster costs ₹13.99 lakh ex-showroom in India and the Dark is expected here in 2027.

subs.headline: Bajaj launches the Pulsar N250SS at ₹1.59 lakh with a TFT console and ride modes
subs.text: The N250SS tops the N250 line-up, ₹14,136 above the standard bike. It gets a 5-inch TFT console with Bluetooth and Google Maps mirroring, plus an electronic throttle body that enables ride modes. It comes in four new colours.

subs.headline: Honda Rebel 300 deliveries start around Dhanteras, with BigWing dealers calling first-batch buyers
subs.text: BigWing dealers are telling buyers that deliveries of both the standard and E-Clutch Rebel 300 begin soon. One E-Clutch buyer was offered delivery on 6 November. The Rebel 300 starts at ₹2.22 lakh; the first batch size is not known.

subs.headline: Harley-Davidson X350T spotted undisguised at a dealership, likely a 349cc version of the X440T
subs.text: The X350T carries its name on the tank, with orange paint, a TFT display and upside-down forks. BikeWale expects a 349cc version of the X440T’s 440cc engine, which would fall under the 18 per cent GST rate, against 40 per cent above 350cc. No price or date is confirmed.
